summary: Equatorial Guinea's restoration and mixed ecosystem pledges include, by 2050, an 80% reduction in deforestation and degradation, rehabilitation of 70% of cocoa and coffee plantations, restoration of 1,300 ha of mangroves alongside conservation of 24,700 ha, and 15,600 trees across 20 cities. The conservation agenda adds 101,276 ha of new terrestrial protected areas; by 2050, 1,307,692 ha of forest will be managed sustainably—about 53.9% of the current 24,277 km² forest area, itself 90.9% of the country—and at least 50% of protected areas will be effectively managed. Agriculture targets 100% production to avoid exports by 2030 and agricultural land reduced to 50%. Other goals reduce forest-operation illegality to 80% by 2030 and protect 50% of coasts by 2050. Associated annual absorption by 2050 is 17,000,000 t CO2 eq from forests, 138,000 t from urban greening, and 344,500 t from mangroves.
